# pbs_notification_endpoint_smtp (Resource)

Manages a Proxmox Backup Server SMTP notification endpoint: a mail server PBS delivers notifications through — about garbage collection, prune, verify and sync jobs, tape backups, package updates and certificates; mails about backups come from Proxmox VE. A notification reaches an endpoint only through a matcher: route notifications to this one with a `pbs_notification_matcher` whose `target` names it, such as the built-in `default-matcher`, imported.

PBS does not contact the server when it saves the endpoint; a wrong setting shows when PBS sends the first notification. Endpoint and matcher names share one namespace.

~> **PBS refuses to delete an endpoint a matcher targets.** When a change of `name` replaces an endpoint that a `pbs_notification_matcher` targets, set `lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }` on the endpoint, so that the matcher moves to the new endpoint before the old one goes.

Managing notification endpoints needs `Sys.Modify on /system/notifications`, reading them `Sys.Audit on /system/notifications`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Mail through a relay that takes STARTTLS on port 587 and wants a sign-in.
# PBS does not contact the relay until it sends the first notification, and
# sends one here only through a matcher that targets the endpoint: see the
# pbs_notification_matcher example, which points the built-in default-matcher
# at it.
resource "pbs_notification_endpoint_smtp" "mail" {
  name         = "smtp"
  server       = "smtp.example.com"
  mode         = "starttls"
  port         = 587
  username     = "pbs@example.com"
  from_address = "pbs@example.com"
  author       = "Backup server"
  mailto       = ["backup-admins@example.com"]

  # The password is write-only: it never reaches the plan or state, and PBS
  # receives it when the endpoint is created and whenever
  # password_wo_version changes.
  password_wo         = var.smtp_password
  password_wo_version = 1
}

variable "smtp_password" {
  description = "Password of pbs@example.com on smtp.example.com."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  ephemeral   = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `from_address` (String) Sender address of the mails. A relay may insist that it belongs to `username`.
- `name` (String) Endpoint name, 2 to 32 characters: letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, not starting with `.` or `-`. Matchers name it in `target`. Changing it replaces the endpoint.
- `server` (String) Host name or IP address of the SMTP server or relay.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `author` (String) Sender name of the mails, which appear from `<author> <from_address>`; `Proxmox Backup Server - <host name>` when left out.
- `comment` (String) Free-form comment, up to 128 characters on one line.
- `disable` (Boolean) Whether the endpoint is disabled: matchers that target it send nothing through it. Defaults to `false`.
- `mailto` (Set of String) Mail addresses to send notifications to. At least one of `mailto` and `mailto_user` is required.
- `mailto_user` (Set of String) Users, such as `root@pam`, to send notifications to, at the email address PBS has for each.
- `mode` (String) Connection security: `tls`, the default, for TLS from the start; `starttls`, to upgrade a plain connection; `insecure`, for none.
- `password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Password to authenticate to the SMTP server with, along with `username`, without white space at either end, which PBS would drop when it reads the password back. Write-only: Terraform passes it to PBS without storing it in the plan or state, and PBS never returns it, so a change made outside Terraform goes unnoticed. PBS receives it when the object is created and whenever `password_wo_version` changes. Requires `password_wo_version`, and Terraform or OpenTofu 1.11 or later.
- `password_wo_version` (Number) Version of `password_wo`, which Terraform stores in its place. Change it — increment it, say — to send a new `password_wo`; removing it, with `password_wo`, leaves the value on the server as it is. Requires `password_wo`.
- `port` (Number) Port of the SMTP server; when left out, the one `mode` implies: 465 for `tls`, 587 for `starttls`, 25 for `insecure`.
- `username` (String) User name to authenticate with, by PLAIN or LOGIN; no authentication when left out. Requires `password_wo`: PBS fails to send with a user name but no password.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same value as `name`, present because Terraform requires an `id`.
- `origin` (String) Where the endpoint comes from: `user-created` for every SMTP endpoint, as PBS has no built-in one.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_notification_endpoint_smtp.mail
  identity = {
    name = "smtp"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `name` (String) Endpoint name, such as `smtp`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_notification_endpoint_smtp.mail
  id = "smtp"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# SMTP endpoints are imported by name. PBS never returns the password, so
# password_wo_version is empty after an import, and a configuration that sets
# it sends password_wo in the next apply, replacing the password PBS has.
terraform import pbs_notification_endpoint_smtp.mail smtp
```
